description: Canonical template-variable vocabulary for configuration snips. A variable is named for the semantic object it parameterizes, not for the textual position it occupies in a CLI statement.
aliasRule: A legacy variable name may be recorded as a global alias only when its semantic intent is unambiguous across known evidence. Ambiguous legacy names are recorded as scoped migration provenance instead.

ASN.use: The routing-options autonomous-system value. Bind independently from peer/customer ASNs and route-target or community administrator fields.

ASN_CUSTOMER.use: The peer-as value for a PE-CE/customer adjacency; distinct from the local device ASN and route-target administrator.

UNIT.intent: Logical-interface unit number, without the parent interface name.
UNIT.use: The unit identifier in an interface definition or reference. It is not inherently a VLAN ID, even when the deployed numbers are equal.

VLAN.use: Identifies a service VLAN or a VLAN tag. It is not interchangeable with a logical-interface unit number merely because the values are equal.

IFD.intent: Interface-device identifier, excluding a logical unit.
IFD.use: Identifies the interface device at the interfaces hierarchy, whether physical, aggregated Ethernet or pseudowire-subscriber. The unit identifier is separate.

ROUTER_ID.intent: Complete router identifier in IPv4 dotted-decimal form.
ROUTER_ID.use: The router-id value at global or routing-instance scope. It is not inherently an assigned interface address and is not an alias of LOOPBACK_V4.

AC_IFL.intent: Full logical attachment-circuit interface identifier, including its unit.
AC_IFL.use: The complete interface reference, such as ae2.1001, not the parent interface device or the unit number alone.
AC_IFL.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-09-24 with one prior snippet use; this establishes a convention rather than documenting an already widespread one. The AC_INTF rename remains separately scheduled, not executed.

INSTANCE_NAME.intent: Identity stem of a service instance.
INSTANCE_NAME.use: The routing-instance name, and the stem from which that service's derived object names are formed (for example PS-${INSTANCE_NAME}-IMPORT, PS-${INSTANCE_NAME}-EXPORT, ${INSTANCE_NAME}_RT, and a per-service community carrying the instance name itself). Do not introduce a separate variable for a name that is a deterministic derivative of this stem.

COLOR_COMMUNITY.use: Name of the community carrying the service transport-colour value. Referenced by policy or by service configuration that consumes that community.

migratedFrom.name: COLOR_COMM
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias. $COLOR_COMM denotes the same object in metro_as_a_service, which is frozen; it converges when that JVD is next revised. $COLOR_LIST in srv6_core_edge is a different object (a list of transport-class colour numbers) and is not related.

LOOPBACK_V4.use: The node's own lo0 IPv4. Retain this name even where the value also supplies a subfield of another object, such as the Administrator subfield of a Route Distinguisher.

LOOPBACK_ANYCAST_V4.use: A loopback address owned by more than one node, so the value repeats across the devices that share it.

LOOPBACK_SR_V4.intent: Segment Routing non-zero IPv4 loopback address.
LOOPBACK_SR_V4.use: The per-node loopback that carries an SR prefix-SID, distinct from the primary loopback. Naming records the intended construct; it does not assert that the address is currently instantiated on lo0.

RD.use: The entire RD is parameterized as one value.

RD_SEED_AUTO.intent: Seed for automatic Route Distinguisher generation.
RD_SEED_AUTO.use: The IPv4 value configured by route-distinguisher-id, used as the Administrator subfield of automatically generated Type 1 RDs. It is not a complete RD, an Assigned Number, or inherently a loopback or router ID. Preserve the independently configured per-device value; do not infer equality with LOOPBACK_V4, ROUTER_ID or TC_EGRESS.
RD_SEED_AUTO.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-09-29. Remains distinct from RD_SEED even if that legacy name is later freed by SRv6 reconciliation. RD_SEED currently supplies the prefix of explicitly configured RDs; Juniper's conflict-avoidance guidance requires that explicit RD IPv4 prefix to differ from the automatic seed. These objects are not interchangeable, and RD_SEED is not an alias. Reference: https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/cli-reference/topics/ref/statement/route-distinguisher-id-edit-routing-options.html

RD_SUB_ADMIN.use: Only when the variable itself represents the RD Administrator subfield. If that subfield is supplied by a variable whose primary intent is broader (for example $LOOPBACK_V4), retain the broader variable.

RD_SUB_ASSIGNED.use: The assigned-number component when the RD components are independently parameterized.

migratedFrom.name: RD_ID
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias: $RD_ID is semantically overloaded across the portfolio (Assigned Number subfield in metro_ethernet_business_services and broadband_edge; route-distinguisher-id seed in srv6_core_edge).

RT_AS.use: The administrator component of a route target, in any statement carrying one: vrf-target, vrf-target import, and a community members target:<administrator>:<assigned-number> definition. Service-scoped, not device-scoped — it varies between services on one node and is frequently not that node's own autonomous-system. Pair it with whichever variable supplies the Assigned Number.

migratedFrom.name: AS_LOCAL
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias: every occurrence was the Administrator subfield of a vrf-target, while the name asserts a device-local AS that the bound values contradict.

migratedFrom.name: L3VPN_RT_AS
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias: the same Administrator subfield. The L3VPN qualifier named the constructs that used it, not a narrower semantic object.

RT_ID.use: The assigned-number component of a route target, independent of the variable supplying the Administrator.

USER_PASS.use: The password a broadband subscriber or auto-configured VLAN presents for authentication, such as `password` under `authentication`. It is a credential: never publish a real value.

DOMAIN_NAME.intent: Domain appended to a generated subscriber username.
DOMAIN_NAME.use: The `domain-name` included in a subscriber username by `username-include`. It is not a DNS server or a system domain-name setting.

USER_PREFIX.intent: Prefix of a generated subscriber username.
USER_PREFIX.use: The `user-prefix` included in a subscriber username by `username-include`.

STATIC_MAC.intent: Static MAC address configured on an interface device.
STATIC_MAC.use: The `mac` statement of an interface device, overriding its hardware address.

SUBSCRIBER_V4_PFX_1.intent: Subscriber IPv4 address prefix, one of an ordered set.
SUBSCRIBER_V4_PFX_1.use: An IPv4 network from which subscriber addresses are assigned or autosensed. Numbered _1.._n when a form carries several; the numbers order the set and carry no other meaning.
SUBSCRIBER_V4_PFX_1.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Covers SUBSCRIBER_V4_PFX_1 through SUBSCRIBER_V4_PFX_4.

SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1.intent: Subscriber IPv6 prefix, one of an ordered set.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1.use: An IPv6 prefix from which subscriber prefixes are assigned or autosensed. Numbered _1.._n when a form carries several; the numbers order the set and carry no other meaning.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Covers SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1 through SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_4.

RR3_V4.intent: IPv4 loopback of the third BGP route reflector a client peers with.
RR3_V4.use: Numbered with RR1_V4 and RR2_V4 for route-reflector neighbors on a client form; the number orders the reflectors and carries no other meaning.
RR3_V4.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. RR1_V4 and RR2_V4 are established in metro_ethernet_business_services.

RADIUS_SERVER_V4.intent: IPv4 address of a RADIUS server.
RADIUS_SERVER_V4.use: The RADIUS server under `access radius-server`, a profile `radius-server`, or `authentication-server`.

RADIUS_SOURCE_V4.intent: IPv4 source address for RADIUS requests.
RADIUS_SOURCE_V4.use: The `source-address` a BNG uses toward a RADIUS server; it is an address on the BNG, not the server.

RADIUS_SECRET.use: The `secret` shared with a RADIUS server. It is a credential: never publish a real value.

NAS_IDENTIFIER.use: The `nas-identifier` a BNG reports in RADIUS requests.

REDUNDANCY_SHARED_KEY.use: The `shared-key` of an interface under subscriber-management redundancy; both BNGs of a redundant pair use the same key. It is a credential: never publish a real value.

SUBSCRIBER_V4_POOL.intent: This BNG's DHCP subscriber IPv4 pool network.
SUBSCRIBER_V4_POOL.use: The `network` of the local DHCPv4 address pool; distinct from SUBSCRIBER_V4_PFX_n, which number every BNG prefix a form carries.

SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW.intent: Gateway address of this BNG's subscriber IPv4 pool.
SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW.use: The pool `router` and DHCP `server-identifier` host address, without a prefix length.

SUBSCRIBER_V4_RANGE_LOW.intent: First address of a subscriber IPv4 pool range.
SUBSCRIBER_V4_RANGE_LOW.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Pairs with SUBSCRIBER_V4_RANGE_HIGH.

SUBSCRIBER_V4_RANGE_HIGH.intent: Last address of a subscriber IPv4 pool range.
SUBSCRIBER_V4_RANGE_HIGH.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Pairs with SUBSCRIBER_V4_RANGE_LOW.

SUBSCRIBER_V6_POOL.intent: This BNG's DHCP subscriber IPv6 pool prefix.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_POOL.use: The `prefix` of the local DHCPv6 address pool; distinct from SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_n, which number every BNG prefix a form carries.

SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_LOW.intent: First address of a subscriber IPv6 pool range.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_LOW.use: The `low` bound of an IPv6 address-pool `range`, with its prefix length.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_LOW.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Pairs with SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_HIGH.

SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_HIGH.intent: Last address of a subscriber IPv6 pool range.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_HIGH.use: The `high` bound of an IPv6 address-pool `range`, with its prefix length.
SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_HIGH.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Pairs with SUBSCRIBER_V6_RANGE_LOW.

PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW_1.intent: Another BNG's subscriber IPv4 gateway, one of an ordered set.
PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW_1.use: A host address installed as a /32 discard route for a subscriber pool served by another BNG. Numbered _1.._n in source order; the numbers carry no other meaning.
PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW_1.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Covers PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW_1 through PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V4_GW_3.

PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1.intent: Another BNG's subscriber IPv6 prefix, one of an ordered set.
PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1.use: A prefix installed as a discard route for a subscriber pool served by another BNG. Numbered _1.._n in source order; the numbers carry no other meaning.
PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Covers PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_1 through PEER_SUBSCRIBER_V6_PFX_3.

NEXT_HOP_V4.intent: Explicit IPv4 next hop set by a routing policy.
NEXT_HOP_V4.use: The address in a policy `then next-hop` action. Not a firewall `next-ip` prefix (NEXT_HOP).

NEXT_HOP_V6.intent: Explicit IPv6 next hop set by a routing policy.
NEXT_HOP_V6.use: The address in a policy `then next-hop` action.

ASN_CUSTOMER_V4.intent: Customer-facing BGP peer AS of the IPv4 neighbor.
ASN_CUSTOMER_V4.use: The `peer-as` of the IPv4 CE neighbor when the IPv4 and IPv6 CE neighbors are in different ASes; otherwise use ASN_CUSTOMER.
ASN_CUSTOMER_V4.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Extends ASN_CUSTOMER; pairs with ASN_CUSTOMER_V6.

ASN_CUSTOMER_V6.intent: Customer-facing BGP peer AS of the IPv6 neighbor.
ASN_CUSTOMER_V6.use: The `peer-as` of the IPv6 CE neighbor when the IPv4 and IPv6 CE neighbors are in different ASes; otherwise use ASN_CUSTOMER.
ASN_CUSTOMER_V6.notes: Ratified by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-07. Extends ASN_CUSTOMER; pairs with ASN_CUSTOMER_V4.

PIM_RP_V4.intent: IPv4 address of a PIM rendezvous point.
PIM_RP_V4.use: The static RP `address` on a receiver, or the local RP `address` on the RP itself.
PIM_RP_V4.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge.

MCAST_GROUP_V4_PFX.use: A PIM RP `group-ranges` entry, a selective provider-tunnel group or a firewall destination that matches multicast groups.
MCAST_GROUP_V4_PFX.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge.

ASN_PROVIDER.intent: Provider autonomous-system number as seen from a CE.
ASN_PROVIDER.use: The `peer-as` a customer router configures toward the provider PEs; the inverse of ASN_CUSTOMER.
ASN_PROVIDER.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge.

PE_PEER_V4.intent: IPv4 address of a provider PE eBGP neighbor, as configured on a CE.
PE_PEER_V4.use: Numbered _1/_2 when a CE peers with several PEs in one group; the numbers follow neighbor order.
PE_PEER_V4.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers PE_PEER_V4_1 and PE_PEER_V4_2.

AC_IFL_A.intent: Attachment-circuit logical interface, one of a lettered set.
AC_IFL_A.use: Extends AC_IFL when one instance, bridge domain or VLAN names several attachment units; _A.._E order the members.
AC_IFL_A.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers AC_IFL_A through AC_IFL_E.

ASN_CUSTOMER_1.intent: Customer-facing BGP peer AS, one of an ordered set.
ASN_CUSTOMER_1.use: Extends ASN_CUSTOMER when one instance peers with several customer routers; the numbers follow the BGP groups.
ASN_CUSTOMER_1.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers ASN_CUSTOMER_1 and ASN_CUSTOMER_2.

BGP_EXPORT_POL.intent: Policy-statement name applied as a BGP `export`.
BGP_EXPORT_POL.use: Numbered _1/_2 for the members of an `export [ … ]` list, in evaluation order.
BGP_EXPORT_POL.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers BGP_EXPORT_POL_1 and BGP_EXPORT_POL_2.

OSPF_EXPORT_POL.intent: Policy-statement name applied as an OSPF `export`.
OSPF_EXPORT_POL.use: The OSPF export policy inside a routing instance.
OSPF_EXPORT_POL.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge.

IBGP_PEER_V4.intent: IPv4 address of an internal BGP neighbor.
IBGP_PEER_V4.use: An iBGP neighbor that is not a route reflector; numbered _1.._n for the neighbors of one group, in neighbor order.
IBGP_PEER_V4.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers IBGP_PEER_V4_1 through IBGP_PEER_V4_5.

IFL.intent: Logical interface identifier, including its unit.
IFL.use: A logical interface named in a protocol or instance stanza where no attachment-circuit or core role is established; numbered _1.._n for an ordered set.
IFL.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers IFL_1 through IFL_3.

INPUT_FILTER.intent: Firewall filter name applied as `filter input`.
INPUT_FILTER.use: The input filter of a logical interface family.
INPUT_FILTER.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge.

LSP_NAME_1.intent: RSVP-TE label-switched-path name, one of an ordered set.
LSP_NAME_1.use: Pairs with LSP_TO_V4_n of the same number.
LSP_NAME_1.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers LSP_NAME_1 through LSP_NAME_3.

LSP_TO_V4_1.intent: Egress (`to`) IPv4 address of a label-switched path, one of an ordered set.
LSP_TO_V4_1.use: Pairs with LSP_NAME_n of the same number.
LSP_TO_V4_1.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers LSP_TO_V4_1 through LSP_TO_V4_3.

MATCH_DEST_V4_PFX_1.intent: Destination IPv4 prefix a firewall term matches, one of an ordered set.
MATCH_DEST_V4_PFX_1.use: A `destination-address` entry of a filter term.
MATCH_DEST_V4_PFX_1.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge. Covers MATCH_DEST_V4_PFX_1 and MATCH_DEST_V4_PFX_2.

MVPN_RT_ID.intent: Route Target Assigned Number of an MVPN route target.
MVPN_RT_ID.use: The tail of the MVPN `route-target` import/export target; the Administrator subfield is RT_AS.
MVPN_RT_ID.notes: Provisionally accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-09; reconciled across EWAN Finance and EWAN Core/Edge.

BGP_GROUP.intent: Name of a BGP peer group.
BGP_GROUP.use: The `group` name of a CE-facing group in a VRF, or of a CE group toward the provider edge, when the name differs between instances. A fixed group name that other configuration references stays literal.
BGP_GROUP.notes: Accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-10; introduced by EWAN Core/Edge.

VRRP_VIP.use: The `virtual-address` of a VRRP group on an attachment unit, shared by the routers of the group.
VRRP_VIP.notes: Accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-10; introduced by EWAN Core/Edge.

VRRP_PRIORITY.intent: VRRP priority of this router in a group.
VRRP_PRIORITY.use: The `priority` of a VRRP group on an attachment unit; the routers of one group carry different values.
VRRP_PRIORITY.notes: Accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-10; introduced by EWAN Core/Edge.

LOOPBACK_VRF_V4.intent: IPv4 address of a VRF loopback unit.
LOOPBACK_VRF_V4.use: The address on the lo0 unit placed in a VRF. Retain this name where the same value also supplies the RD Administrator subfield or the local PIM RP address in that VRF.
LOOPBACK_VRF_V4.notes: Accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-10; introduced by EWAN Core/Edge.

MCAST_SOURCE_V4_PFX.use: The `source` of a selective provider-tunnel (S,G) entry.
MCAST_SOURCE_V4_PFX.notes: Accepted by Kevin Brown on 2026-10-10; introduced by EWAN Core/Edge.

notes: RD encoding (2-byte ASN, IPv4 address, or 4-byte ASN administrator) is per-occurrence evidence, not part of the variable name. Do not introduce $RD_ASN2, $RD_ASN4, or $RD_FIELD1 unless a construct genuinely requires that semantic distinction.

$RD_SEED_AUTO is the canonical automatic-RD seed. Legacy $RD_ID in that operand position remains scoped migration evidence, not a global alias; no legacy snippet rename is implied by this registration.
